docs.title: Workload Spec Schema
docs.text: Complete YAML schema reference for BLIS workload specifications (--workload-spec). For a guide-level introduction, see Workload Specifications.

docs.title: Top-Level Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description version string No Schema version ("2" recommended; "1" auto-upgraded) seed int64 No RNG seed (overridden by CLI --seed if set) category string No language, multimodal, reasoning, or empty aggregate_rate float64 Yes Total arrival rate in requests/second num_requests int64 No Total requests to generate (0 = unlimited, use horizon) horizon int64 No Simulation time limit in ticks (overridden by CLI --horizon if set) clients list Yes* Client specifications (see below) cohorts list No Cohort specifications with population dynamics (diurnal, spike, drain patterns) servegen_data object No Native ServeGen data file loading inference_perf object No inference-perf format compatibility

*At least one client, cohort, or servegen_data is required.

docs.title: Client Specification
docs.text:
Each entry in the clients list defines a traffic source:

Field Type Required Description id string No Client identifier (for metrics grouping) tenant_id string No Tenant identifier slo_class string No SLO tier: critical, standard, sheddable, batch, background, or empty model string No Model name override (for multi-model workloads) rate_fraction float64 Yes Fraction of aggregate_rate for this client (must be positive). When lifecycle windows are present, fractions are normalized per-phase (see Lifecycle Normalization) arrival object Yes Arrival process configuration input_distribution object Yes Input token length distribution output_distribution object Yes Output token length distribution prefix_group string No Prefix group name (requests in same group share prefixes) prefix_length int No Shared prefix token count (additive to input_distribution) streaming bool No Whether to simulate streaming output network object No Client-side network characteristics lifecycle object No Activity window configuration multimodal object No Multimodal token generation reasoning object No Reasoning multi-turn behavior timeout int64 No Per-request timeout in µs. nil = default (300s for sessions). 0 = no timeout slo_target_us int64 No Per-request SLO TTFT target in µs. nil/0 = no target. Carried on the request and into exported TraceV2 files, and sent to the embedded llm-d router as the x-llm-d-slo-ttft-ms header (whole milliseconds, rounded up), which its slo-deadline-ordering-policy reads (see Routing)

docs.title: Arrival Process
docs.text: Field Type Values Description process string poisson, gamma, weibull, constant Inter-arrival time distribution cv *float64 Required for gamma and weibull Coefficient of variation (burstiness). CV > 1 = bursty, CV < 1 = regular

docs.title: Distribution Specification
docs.text:
Used for input_distribution and output_distribution:

Field Type Description type string gaussian, exponential, pareto_lognormal, lognormal, constant, empirical params map Type-specific parameters (see below) file string Reserved for future use (file-based loading not yet implemented). Use inline params instead.

docs.title: Distribution Parameters
docs.text: Type Parameters gaussian mean, std_dev, min, max exponential mean pareto_lognormal alpha, xm, mu, sigma, mix_weight lognormal mu, sigma (mean and standard deviation of log-transformed values; fitted via method of moments) constant value empirical inline params map (key=token count, value=probability)

docs.title: Network Specification
docs.text: Field Type Description rtt_ms float64 Round-trip time in milliseconds bandwidth_mbps float64 Bandwidth in Mbps

docs.title: Reasoning Specification
docs.text: Field Type Description reason_ratio_distribution DistSpec Distribution of reasoning-to-output ratio multi_turn object Multi-turn conversation configuration multi_turn.max_rounds int Maximum conversation rounds multi_turn.think_time_us int64 User think time between rounds (microseconds) multi_turn.context_growth string accumulate (prepend prior context) or empty (fixed-length) multi_turn.single_session bool If true, each client creates exactly one session instead of spawning new sessions per arrival. Used by inference-perf multi-turn expansion. Default: false

docs.title: Cohort Specification
docs.text:
Each entry in the cohorts list defines a population with lifecycle dynamics. Cohorts expand into individual clients with lifecycle windows derived from diurnal, spike, or drain patterns.

Field Type Required Description id string No Cohort identifier population int Yes Number of clients in this cohort (max 100,000) tenant_id string No Tenant identifier slo_class string No SLO tier: critical, standard, sheddable, batch, background model string No Model name override arrival object Yes Arrival process configuration (same as Client) input_distribution object Yes Input token length distribution output_distribution object Yes Output token length distribution prefix_group string No Prefix group name prefix_sharing string No "shared" (default): all members share one prefix. "per_member": each member gets its own prefix. Requires prefix_group. streaming bool No Whether to simulate streaming output rate_fraction float64 Yes Fraction of aggregate_rate for each client in this cohort diurnal object No Sinusoidal rate modulation (see below) spike object No Traffic spike configuration (see below) drain object No Linear ramp-down to zero (see below) timeout int64 No Per-request timeout in µs (same as Client) slo_target_us int64 No Per-request SLO TTFT target in µs (same as Client)

docs.title: Diurnal Pattern
docs.text: Field Type Description peak_hour int Hour of peak traffic (0-23) peak_to_trough_ratio float64 Ratio of peak to trough rate (≥ 1.0)

docs.title: Spike Pattern
docs.text: Field Type Description start_time_us int64 Spike start time in microseconds duration_us int64 Spike duration in microseconds trace_rate float64 Cohort-level arrival rate in req/s (required when aggregate_rate: 0); divided evenly across population members

docs.title: Drain Pattern
docs.text: Field Type Description start_time_us int64 Drain start time in microseconds ramp_duration_us int64 Ramp-down duration in microseconds

docs.title: Lifecycle Specification
docs.text:
Activity window configuration for clients (used in the lifecycle field of Client Specification). Cohort patterns (diurnal, spike, drain) are converted into lifecycle windows internally.

Field Type Description windows list List of active time windows

docs.title: Active Window
docs.text: Field Type Description start_us int64 Window start time in microseconds end_us int64 Window end time in microseconds trace_rate float64 Per-window rate override. In absolute rate mode (aggregate_rate: 0), this is the absolute arrival rate (req/s). In proportional mode, this is a weight for rate allocation. arrival ArrivalSpec Per-window arrival process override (overrides client-level arrival) input_distribution DistSpec Per-window input token distribution override (overrides client-level input_distribution) output_distribution DistSpec Per-window output token distribution override (overrides client-level output_distribution)

docs.title: Lifecycle Normalization
docs.text:
Proportional mode (aggregate_rate > 0): When clients have lifecycle windows, rate_fraction values are normalized per-phase rather than globally. For each client, the simulator sums the rate_fraction of all co-active clients (those whose lifecycle windows overlap) and divides by that sum. This ensures aggregate_rate is achieved during every active phase.

Absolute rate mode (aggregate_rate = 0): Each window's trace_rate is used directly as the arrival rate (requests/second) for that window, without scaling or normalization. This mode preserves time-varying aggregate load patterns from traces (e.g., ServeGen workloads) where the aggregate rate varies over time. Validation requires all rate-based clients to have explicit trace_rate on every window.

Clients without lifecycle windows are "always-on" and are counted as co-active with every phase.

Example: A two-phase workload with aggregate_rate: 40:

  • Phase 1 (0–50s): clients A (rate_fraction: 0.7) and B (rate_fraction: 0.3)
  • Phase 2 (50–100s): client C (rate_fraction: 1.0)

Each phase's fractions are normalized independently: A gets 40 × 0.7/1.0 = 28 req/s, B gets 40 × 0.3/1.0 = 12 req/s, C gets 40 × 1.0/1.0 = 40 req/s. Both phases produce the full 40 req/s.

Without per-phase normalization, the global sum would be 2.0, and every client's rate would be halved.

Limitation: Always-on clients compute a single rate using co-active sums across all phases they overlap with. When an always-on client coexists with multiple non-overlapping phased clients, per-phase totals may be less than aggregate_rate. For predictable results, use either all-phased or all-always-on clients.

docs.title: Multimodal Specification
docs.text:
Configures multimodal request generation (used in the multimodal field of Client Specification). Each distribution follows the same Distribution Specification format.

Field Type Description text_distribution DistSpec Text token distribution image_distribution DistSpec Image token distribution image_count_distribution DistSpec Number of images per request audio_distribution DistSpec Audio token distribution audio_count_distribution DistSpec Number of audio segments per request video_distribution DistSpec Video token distribution video_count_distribution DistSpec Number of video segments per request

docs.title: ServeGen Data Specification
docs.text:
Native ServeGen data file loading (used in the servegen_data top-level field):

Field Type Required Description path string Yes Path to ServeGen data directory (containing chunk-*-trace.csv and dataset.json) time_window string No Temporal snapshot extraction: midnight (0:00-0:30), morning (8:00-8:30), or afternoon (14:00-14:30). Filters chunks to the specified 30-minute window. span_start int64 No Trace span start filter (microseconds) span_end int64 No Trace span end filter (microseconds)

docs.title: InferencePerf Specification
docs.text:
inference-perf format compatibility (used in the inference_perf top-level field):

Field Type Required Description stages list Yes Rate/duration stages for load patterns shared_prefix object Yes Shared prefix expansion configuration

docs.title: Stage
docs.text: Field Type Description rate float64 Requests per second for this stage duration int64 Stage duration in seconds (note: unlike other time fields which use microseconds, this field uses seconds)

docs.title: Shared Prefix
docs.text: Field Type Description num_unique_system_prompts int Number of unique system prompts num_users_per_system_prompt int Users per system prompt system_prompt_len int System prompt length in tokens question_len int Question length in tokens output_len int Output length in tokens enable_multi_turn_chat bool When true, maps to BLIS reasoning.multi_turn with SingleSession mode and fixed-length inputs (no context accumulation). Computes MaxRounds and ThinkTimeUs from stage parameters. See #514.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
version: "2"
seed: 42
category: reasoning
aggregate_rate: 500.0
num_requests: 500

clients:
  - id: "multi-turn-chat"
    tenant_id: "chat-users"
    slo_class: "standard"
    rate_fraction: 1.0
    streaming: true
    arrival:
      process: poisson
    input_distribution:
      type: gaussian
      params:
        mean: 128
        std_dev: 30
        min: 32
        max: 512
    output_distribution:
      type: gaussian
      params:
        mean: 64
        std_dev: 20
        min: 16
        max: 256
    reasoning:
      reason_ratio_distribution:
        type: gaussian
        params:
          mean: 0
          std_dev: 0
          min: 0
          max: 0
      multi_turn:
        max_rounds: 5
        think_time_us: 500000
        context_growth: accumulate

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
BLIS validates workload specs with strict YAML parsing (KnownFields(true)) — typos in field names cause errors. Additional validation:

  • aggregate_rate must be positive
  • Each client's rate_fraction must be positive
  • arrival.process must be one of the valid processes
  • cv for gamma/weibull must be finite and positive
  • Weibull cv must be in [0.01, 10.4]
  • Distribution types must be recognized
  • All numeric params must be finite (no NaN or Inf)
  • At least one client, cohort, or servegen_data is required
  • Cohort population must be positive and ≤ 100,000

How close BLIS's predictions are to measured serving runs, anchor by anchor. Each anchor is one measured deployment and workload that BLIS replays as it ran.

No anchor is EXACT

Every comparison below has at least one configuration or workload difference that this build cannot remove (a different vLLM version, benchmark-client fork, or unrecorded setting). The errors are reported per anchor with those differences listed; none is used to fit coefficients. An anchor becomes EXACT when its configuration and workload diff is empty and no provenance row is MISMATCH or UNVERIFIABLE: each page says what that would take.

docs.title: Verdicts
docs.text:
• EXACT: the diff between the run and the BLIS replay is empty, and every setting is stated by the run.
  • PARTIAL: scored, but with differences listed per anchor; some are removable (the run did not record a setting), some are not (BLIS cannot express it).
  • NOT_REPRODUCIBLE: the run cannot be replayed as it ran (no engine log, model not in the catalog, or similar); not scored.

docs.title: Error definitions
docs.text:
• Signed error per point: 100 * (BLIS / measured - 1). Its sign is the bias direction; the sign row says whether it holds at every level.
  • MAPE: mean absolute signed error over points.
  • Shape error: each side divided by its own lowest-load value, then the same error, excluding the lowest level. It removes a constant level offset and keeps how the metric moves with load.
  • KV-pool ratio: BLIS's KV-cache pool divided by the pool vLLM logged at start-up.

Output metrics (output tok/s, ITL/TPOT, interactivity) come first on every page, TTFT second.

docs.title: Provenance verdict
docs.text:
Every arm is PARTIAL. The deployment matches field for field (TP, EP, max-num-seqs, capture size, max-num-batched-tokens, gpu-memory-utilization, max-model-len, block size, CUDA graph mode, Engram CPU offload, speculative settings), and the corpus, scenario, seed and window are the run's. These differences remain:

setting measured run BLIS verdict note vLLM image vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-cd10ed6f9f6b37a8ace9cf380007e66fe12ec0c3 kernel engine behaviour v0.31.0 (blis-latency-kernel new.go:2517) MISMATCH (not removable) server log: vLLM 0.29.1rc1.dev128+gcd10ed6f9 aiperf harness aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp aiperf release 0.12.0 transcription MISMATCH (not removable) fork differs from release in agentic_replay.py, weka_trace.py, branch_orchestrator.py, replay_dependencies.py; metric formulas unchanged trace idle-gap cap --trace-idle-gap-cap-seconds 300 unset (schema refuses) MISMATCH (not removable) inactive at c1 (0 'Per-trace idle cap advanced' lines), active at c>=2 cache-pressure warmup --warmup-requests-per-lane 10 synthesized only MISMATCH (not removable) compilation mode NONE no field (kernel prices CUDA-graph replay) UNSTATED torch.compile disabled in the run (mode NONE); graphs FULL_AND_PIECEWISE frontend/runner env Rust frontend launched (server log) not modelled UNSTATED

Population metrics at concurrency ≥ 2 are confounded by the idle-gap cap: it raises the offered load the run saw beyond what BLIS replays. The comparison that survives every mismatch is the request-level pairing: the same request on both sides, with the same number of requests in flight.

What would make it EXACT: a run on the vLLM release whose behaviour the kernel prices (v0.31.0), or kernel pricing for the nightly that ran; the aiperf release BLIS transcribes (0.12.0), or a transcription of the fork; blis-schemas Replay support for the per-trace idle-gap cap and per-lane warm-up requests, or a run without them; and the UNSTATED rows stated by the run.

docs.title: Provenance verdict
docs.text:
verdict sweeps model families EXACT 0 -- PARTIAL 68 deepseek-v4, gpt-oss, kimi, minimax NOT_REPRODUCIBLE 45 llama

No sweep is EXACT. Every PARTIAL sweep left at least one engine setting unpassed, so the harness used the value vLLM resolves for it (tier MEASURED-OR-RESOLVED). Unpassed settings, by number of PARTIAL sweeps:

setting sweeps block_size 48 enable_prefix_caching 1 max_num_batched_tokens 11 max_num_seqs 31

NOT_REPRODUCIBLE sweeps have no engine-args log, so the settings they passed are unknown, and their sent prompt lengths are not verified equal to the replayed targets. They enter only the ALL (approximate) tier below, and no conclusion. The workload is single-turn random ISL/OSL, not agentic.

What would make a sweep EXACT (tier STRICT): an engine-args log at every concurrency, every admission setting passed by the run rather than left to vLLM's default, and the sent prompt lengths verified.

docs.text:
BLIS binaries these results describe

Public llm-d benchmark results (llm-d-prism and the gs://llm-d-benchmarks bucket) for models in blis-catalog, replayed by BLIS.

Signed error 100 * (BLIS / measured - 1): positive means BLIS is higher (slower latency, or more throughput). Geo-mean bias is 100 * (exp(mean log ratio) - 1).

docs.title: Provenance verdict
docs.text: No Prism run is EXACT (0 EXACT anchors). Every run on a catalog model leaves material settings unstated (vLLM version, serve args, router config, offload size) with no run artifact that resolves them, so each anchor is PARTIAL (the source analysis calls it APPROXIMATE).

docs.title: A1: PARTIAL
docs.text:
Llama-3.1-70B on H100, standalone vLLM (14 replica x TP configs, concurrency 1 to 256, random 10000/1000).

Source: llm-d-prism archive at 6769be260f44; serve args from llm-d-benchmark 58b2d1b.

  • vLLM image vllm-openai:latest on the run dates (v0.10.1.1 or v0.10.2); BLIS prices v0.31.0 behaviour
  • serve args reconstructed from the benchmark repo plus vLLM v0.10.2 defaults; the replica x TP treatment list is in no commit
  • routing is a Kubernetes Service (connection-level random); BLIS uses round-robin
  • the archive keeps no p90 and no per-request data; output tok/s is derived from the request rate

docs.title: A2: PARTIAL
docs.text:
Llama-3.1-70B on H100, P/D through llm-d (5 prefill/decode layouts), as recorded (disaggregated).

Source: same archive; llm-d-benchmark e98acd0.

  • all of A1's differences
  • llm-d image tag auto (vLLM version unknown); gpu-memory-utilization not passed
  • router plugins-v2.yaml on inference-scheduler v0.2.1, which BLIS's EPP config cannot ingest, with no P/D profile handler
  • NIXL over TCP; BLIS uses a nominal 100GbE fabric; BLIS pools cannot share a node

docs.title: A2': PARTIAL
docs.text:
The same P/D runs modelled as colocated replicas (hypothesis: the measured runs did not disaggregate).

Source: same as A2.

  • all of A2's differences
  • the mixed-TP layout is omitted

docs.title: B: PARTIAL
docs.text:
Llama-3.3-70B on H100, 4 x TP4, shared-prefix 30k/50k/70k at concurrency 20, with prefix-cache offloading.

Source: 7 curated reports in the public bucket gs://llm-d-benchmarks/prefix-cache-offloading/.

  • model graph is Llama-3.1-70B's (architecture-identical config)
  • LMCache and llm-d-fs offload are not modelled; the CPU tier size is unstated
  • the EPP plugin config is unstated, so two BLIS routings bracket it
  • vLLM version unknown (llm-d-cuda v0.5.1/v0.6.0); the input length is the measured mean

What would make a run EXACT: the vLLM version, serve args and router config recorded with the run, an EPP version BLIS can ingest, and (for B) an offload connector BLIS models with its CPU tier size stated.
